inputs.text: More than 58 lakh names were deleted from West Bengal’s electoral rolls, yet the tribunals meant to hear challenges are still not operational—even after the Supreme Court directed their creation. The software is ready, but basic arrangements, including where the tribunals will sit, are still being discussed by the state government and Calcutta High Court. When so many people risk losing their vote, delays in setting up a meaningful appeal process are not a minor administrative issue: they leave people, especially those with the least power to navigate bureaucracy, waiting to defend a fundamental right.
